egress.terms: Every KVM Slice plan on the vendor page is listed 'Unmetered Bandwidth' and the High Volume plans 'Unlim. 1000 Mbps'; no numeric transfer cap is published on the vendor pages read. No fair-use rule tied to the memory of the slice is stated on the vendor pages read.
egress.free_allowance: unmetered; no numeric transfer cap is published on the vendor pages read

interface_detail: block (attach as disk), then sftp/rsync/nfs from the slice
tooling: Anything. It is a raw block device on a KVM slice.
chaining: Hot-pluggable between slices in the same facility with no reboot, which makes it easy to re-front with a different server. No object API at all ('We may consider an Object Store product down the line, but not at this time').
limits_note: Per-object-cap: none. Downgrade impossible. You must order a new slab and migrate. 10 TB hard cap per slab. Requires a base slice, so the true entry cost is a slice plus a slab.

identity_cost.detail: Registration needs a legitimate name and surname and a residential address, placed from a residential ISP; a phone number is not required; payment by PayPal, credit card, cryptocurrency (Coinpayments) or Alipay, with account details matching the payment method.

reliability_note: Frantech, operating since 2010, the most consistently recommended block-storage product on LET for a decade. Known friction: signup must come from a residential ISP and is refused from VPN/Tor/datacenter IPs, P.O. boxes rejected. A real obstacle for a privacy-conscious buyer but not an identity-document requirement. Storage is 'enterprise 7200RPM hard drives with an NVME cache and a 40Gbit+ InfiniBand'.

extras.verified_at_basis: re-read on 2026-11-03 against https://buyvm.net/block-storage-slabs/, https://buyvm.net/kvm-dedicated-server-slices/ and https://buyvm.net/terms-of-service/ (which states the residential-ISP registration rule); the third-party forum rows on bandwidth rules stay unverified: the vendor pages state no such rule
extras.quota_verbatim: Sold in 256 GB chunks at $1.25/mo. Max 10 TB per Slab, max 8 Slabs per KVM Slice = 80 TB theoretical. Requires an accompanying KVM slice in the same facility. Available Las Vegas, New York, Miami, Luxembourg.
extras.limits_verbatim: per-object-cap: none. Downgrade impossible — you must order a new slab and migrate. 10 TB hard cap per slab. Requires a base slice, so the true entry cost is a slice plus a slab.
extras.egress_verbatim: 'Unmetered Bandwidth' on every slice, governed by a fair-use rule the company states publicly on LET: 'The rule-of-thumb for WAN (internet-facing connections) is 100Mbit/s of 24/7 usage per every 4GB of memory with a purchased slice. We do, however, allow our customers to burst their usage up to 1Gbit/s during times of lower network use.' A second formulation from a customer cites 'FUP is 25 Mbps per 1GB of RAM for the 95th percentile'. So the storage is metered-free but the sustained rate is tied to how much RAM you bought — on the $3.50/mo 1 GB slice that is ~25 Mbps sustained, i.e. ~8 TB/mo. Internal traffic between services in the same location is genuinely unmetered and unbilled.
extras.chaining_verbatim: Hot-pluggable between slices in the same facility with no reboot, which makes it easy to re-front with a different server. No object API at all ('We may consider an Object Store product down the line, but not at this time').
extras.tooling_verbatim: anything — it is a raw block device on a KVM slice
extras.interface_verbatim: block (attach as disk), then sftp/rsync/nfs from the slice
extras.price_verbatim: $5.00/TB/mo flat, plus the base slice. At 5 TB: $25/mo slab + $3.50 slice = $28.50/mo = $5.70/TB all-in. At 20 TB: 2x 10 TB slabs = $100/mo + $3.50 = $103.50/mo = $5.18/TB. The all-in figure is what matters and it is worse than the headline because the slice is mandatory overhead.
extras.agent_focus: cheap-PAID lane — cheapest $/TB/month storage outside Europe for a self-funded buyer. Every candidate priced at the 5 TB and 20 TB tier as $ per TB per month, egress policy quoted verbatim, and payment friction for a non-US/non-EU buyer recorded. Deliberately excludes AWS/Azure/GCP/Alibaba/R2/B2/iDrive e2 (rejected). FX rates used throughout, taken 2026-10-21 from api.frankfurter.dev: EUR 0.89015, CAD 1.4046, INR 94.47, JPY 157.88, KRW 1325.57 per USD.

binding_note: the per-object cap sets the shard size and therefore the object count; it bounds the total more tightly than any headline quota
